question.leadin: Answer some questions about the ancient city of Babylon.
question.text: This ruler of Babylon is known for his harsh law code, which served as one of the earliest law codes in history and used the principle of "an eye for an eye" and "a tooth for a tooth".
question.clue: This Amorite king went up a mountain to receive a stele from the sun god Shamash that was later discovered in Susa.

swap.leadin: The sun god Shamash [SHAH-mahsh] is depicted on a black basalt monument giving this set of laws to its namesake.
swap.text: Name this Akkadian legal code engraved on a stele [STEE-lee] that is named for a Babylonian king. It has 282 laws, including the well-known ones about an eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth.
swap.clue: Jean-Vincent Scheil discovered most of it at Susa in 1901, on a stela which also depicts its namesake on the Shamash throne and is written in cuneiform.

question.text: The Sumerians invented textbooks while teaching scribes this Mesopotamian writing system at the eduba. This writing system was designed for reeds to be pressed into clay tablets.
question.clue: Henry Rawlinson studied the Behistun Inscription for insight into this system, which is seen on the oldest complaint tablet.

swap.text: Two Akkadian-speaking empires followed the original Akkadian empire. They were Babylon and this empire centered at Nineveh.
swap.clue: Major rulers of this empire included Tiglath-Pilesar III and Sennacherib.

question.text: This Neo-Assyrian ruler's destructive conquest of Elam is sometimes considered genocide. This ruler's namesake library, discovered by Austen Henry Layard, contained the Epic of Gilgamesh.
question.clue: He had earlier conquered the Elamite capital Susa, and that defeat of the Kushite armies near Memphis allowed him to take the Egyptian capital.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about ancient rulers who name cylinders.
swap.text: Queen Puabi of this civilization's city of Ur was identified by several cylinder seals in her tomb, which was excavated by Leonard Wolley. This civilization developed the Epic of Gilgamesh during the Uruk period.

question.leadin: This was the first empire of the ancient world.
question.text: Name this empire which reached its peak under Naram-Sin and fell to the Gutian invasions. The Elamites wererivals of this empire.
question.clue: Its most famous ruler's life was detailed on the Ebla tablets, and started out as a cup-bearer to Ur-Zababa of Kish.

swap.text: Leonard and Katherine Woolley excavated several royal tombs in this Sumerian city-state. This city's Ziggurat (ZI-gur-aht) was discovered by John George Taylor.
swap.clue: A king named -Nammu, who founded a dynasty that supplanted Lagash and the Gutians, was succeeded by Shulgi.

question.leadin: Although not Moses, one story about this ruler's birth sees his high priestess mother put him into a basket to flow down a river eventually to Ishtar.
question.text: Name this father of Enheduanna, Rimush, Manishtushu who conquered Uruk from Lugal-Zage-Si and eventually all of Sumeria. He also conquered up to the Cedar Forest, or modern day Lebanon. His empire fell within 100 years of his death after Zagros barbarians called the Gutians invaded.
question.answerHtml: Sargon the Great [accept Sargon of Akkad; Note: do not say 2nd answer if they don’t answer with that answer]
question.clue: He appointed his daughter Enheduanna high priestess, and his empire reached its greatest expanse under his grandson Naram-sin.

swap.leadin: The largest remains of one of these structures can be found at Chonga Zanbil, which was built by the Elamites.
swap.text: Name these terraced religious buildings. A seven-storied example called the Etemenanki, which was dedicated to the god Marduk, got a reference in Herodotus's histories.
swap.clue: Koldewey also found one that he took to be a temple to Marduk, the name of which, Etemenanki, translates as "The Foundation of Heaven and Earth."

question.leadin: The rise of this civilization was preceded by the Ubaid period.
question.text: Name this civilization, in which the Epic of Gilgamesh was first composed on cuneiform tablets. This civilization built stepped ziggurats at cities like Nippur and Uruk.
question.answerHtml: Sumer [or sag̃-gíg; accept Sumerian civilization; accept Sumeria; prompt on Mesopotamia or Mesopotamian civilization]
question.clue: This civilisation was conquered by the Akkadians around 2270 BC, but its language continued in sacral use, written in cuneiform.

swap.text: Dally claims the Hanging Gardens were really built in this city, as evidenced by retranslated inscriptions and a bas-relief showing a terraced garden. Sennacherib brought this capital of the Neo-Assyrian Empire to regional prominence.
swap.clue: It's not Palmyra, but ISIS destroyed this city's Temple of Nebu in 2016, in addition to a shrine dedicated to the prophet Jonah.

question.leadin: In 1852, Hormuzd Rassam discovered a second section of this institution in the Ottoman Vilayet of Mosul.
question.text: Name this collection whose discovery is attributed to Assyriologist Austen Layard. This collection found at the site of Nineveh included copies of the Enuma Elish and Poor Man of Nippur.
question.clue: Like a similar institution at Tell el-Amarna, this institution preserved one of the only known versions of "Adapa and the South Wind" as well as several objects "baked" in a post-Carcemish sack.

swap.leadin: In one tomb, this archaeologist discovered a headdress made of golden leaves, four stringed lyres, and a golden and lapis lazuli encrusted bull's head.
swap.text: Name this British archaeologist who in 1922 led an excavation of the Sumerian city of Ur.
swap.clue: This archaeologist made a name for himself by discovering the Great Ziggurat and other buildings at Ur, a Sumerian city then thought to be the world's oldest.

question.leadin: A source describing gifts sent by heads of state during the Late Bronze Age is a letter this kingdom's ruler, Tushratta, sent to Egypt.
question.text: Name this Hurrian-speaking kingdom thought to be ruled from Washakunni by a class called the Maryannu, who spoke an Indo-European language different from their subjects.
question.clue: Based on terms in the Kikkuli horse-training manual, the names of several rulers, and a list of deities found in a treaty, the rulers of this polity are argued to have been Indo-Europeans.

swap.text: The Commagene capital of Samosata was located on the banks of this river. This river and the Tigris River provided sustenance to Mesopotamian civilizations.
swap.clue: Yazid I of the Umayyads defeated a small army belonging to Muhammad's grandson at Karbala, which is near this river. This river roughly parallels the Tigris River.

question.text: Several Chaldaean leaders, including Marduk-apla-usur and Eriba-Marduk, ruled over this kingdom in the 8th century B.C. Nebuchadnezzar II ruled during the "Chaldean dynasty" of a "Neo-" empire of this kingdom.
question.clue: A raid from its western neighbors left it in the hands of the Kassites, and part of it was destroyed by Sennacherib but later rebuilt by his son Essarhadon.

swap.leadin: For 1 + 9 points each, answer the following about the ways ancient mathematicians wrote calculations with or without the number 0.
swap.text: Babylonian mathematicians and astronomers used a complex system which sets what number as a base? Because they lacked a zero numeral, this number and 1 were written the same way.

question.text: The Akkadian dynasty was founded by Sargon, who rose to prominence as cupbearer to Urzababa, the king of this city. Just east of Babylon, this was the traditional first capital of Sumeria after the "Great Flood" and the king of its first dynasty is recorded as Jushur.
question.clue: Kugbau, the grandmother of a famous ruler of this city and one-time alewife, is the first known woman to rule in her own name in Mesopotamia.

swap.leadin: This kingdom's capital was Washukanni. FTPE.
swap.text: Name this Ancient Near Eastern Empire, noted for its rivalry with the Hittites, Assyrians, and Egyptians.
swap.clue: Thutmose IV proposed seven times to marry a princess of this polity, and some scholars have identified Nefertiti with a princess of this polity named Tadukhipa.
